subject: representation-level class unlearning
statement: The paper shows that representation-level forgetting is primarily governed by gradient concentration and representation geometry rather than the identity of saliency-selected weights.

subject: forget gradients in unlearning
statement: The paper reports that forget gradients are strongly concentrated in the final network layers, approximately 92% of the squared gradient energy on CIFAR-10 before any mask is applied.

subject: saliency masks in class unlearning
statement: The paper finds that saliency masks show limited class specificity (specificity index 0.09-0.11), selecting highly overlapping parameter subsets across different forget classes.

subject: NetSim supply chain optimization
statement: The paper reports that NetSim optimized end-to-end services for over 20,000 suppliers at JD.com, reducing the cross-regional fulfillment rate from 6.1% to 4.9%.

subject: simulation-based supply chain planning
statement: The paper reports that average monthly carbon reduction from NetSim optimization is approximately 5,745 tCO2e.

subject: emergent misalignment in fine-tuning
statement: The paper finds that narrow fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct recruits a persona structure present in the model before fine-tuning exists.

subject: subspace projection preventing misalignment
statement: The paper shows that projecting the persona subspace out of the residual stream throughout fine-tuning prevents broad misalignment from 27.7% to 0.0% of judged generations.

subject: persona subspace injection inducing misalignment
statement: The paper reports that injecting the persona subspace into the never-fine-tuned model induces misalignment that grows with dose to 45.4%.

subject: Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding
statement: The paper introduces HOPE, a mathematical framework that models individual neurons as rank-1 Hilbert-Schmidt operators to unify pruning and neuron merging as low-rank subspace projection.

subject: HOPE compression framework
statement: The paper proposes that HOPE is a data-free and hyperparameter-free framework for network compression and fine-tuning.

subject: DINOde vision-text alignment
statement: The paper proposes DINOde, an ODE-based framework that continuously aligns CLIP text embeddings with the DINO visual manifold using Semantic Text Flow and Global Context Flow.

subject: open-vocabulary semantic segmentation
statement: The paper shows that DINOde consistently outperforms existing methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple open-vocabulary semantic segmentation benchmarks.

subject: Mean-to-Score discrete diffusion
object: M2S predicts posterior mean to score
statement: The paper introduces Mean-to-Score (M2S), which predicts a clean-token posterior mean and converts it to the score through an exact kernel-dependent linear map.

subject: CIFAR-10 generative modeling
statement: The paper reports that M2S lowers test BPD from 3.173 to 3.129 on CIFAR-10 (28.4M-parameter model).

subject: OpenWebText language modeling
statement: The paper reports that a 170M-parameter M2S model trained on 262B OpenWebText tokens reaches generative PPL 143.3 at 128 steps.

subject: SeeExplainer graph neural network interpretation
statement: The paper proposes SeeExplainer, a parameter-free explainer for interpreting GNNs using a granular-ball graph refinement mechanism to capture synergistic effects among edges.

subject: GNN explainability on graph classification
statement: The paper shows that SeeExplainer outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on several graph classification datasets.

subject: multimodal EEG foundation model
statement: The paper develops a multimodal EEG foundation model combining a Mamba-based raw signal encoder, a Vision Transformer-style encoder for time-frequency data, and a lightweight text encoder.

subject: seizure detection on CHB-MIT benchmark
statement: The paper reports that on the standard CHB-MIT split, the best single model achieved AUROC 0.874, and an ensemble variant reached 0.878 AUROC, representing state-of-the-art performance.

subject: leave-one-subject-out seizure detection
statement: The paper reports a mean leave-one-subject-out balanced accuracy of 0.558 across 19 subjects for patient-independent seizure detection.

subject: Vision-Only Long-Horizon Navigation
statement: The paper introduces VoLN-UAV, a 7,210-episode benchmark for aerial navigation combining long-horizon goal-directed flight, continuous 3D motion, and context-dependent beacon selection.

subject: vision-only navigation success rates
statement: The paper reports that VoLN-MLLM baseline obtains success rates of 7.4%, 4.5%, and 1.8% on Easy, Normal, and Hard episodes respectively on the five-environment Test-Unseen split.

subject: ResponseGuard vision-language safety guard
statement: The paper proposes ResponseGuard, which reads a harmful verdict from a single pooled representation of request, response, and image in one forward pass without reasoning.

subject: vision-language guardrail performance
statement: The paper shows that ResponseGuard (2B) outperforms a recent 3B reasoning-based vision-language guard on response harmfulness detection without reasoning and at approximately 150 times lower time cost.

subject: MSBraM multi-scale EEG foundation model
statement: The paper proposes MSBraM with a two-stage pretraining framework using a multi-scale neural tokenizer and curriculum multi-scale masking strategy to learn hierarchical EEG representations.

subject: MSBraM EEG foundation model training
statement: The paper reports that MSBraM is pretrained on over 2,400 hours of EEG data and achieves superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art pretrained models.

subject: JITAI-Twins digital twins for health
statement: The paper proposes JITAI-Twins using a conditional time-series diffusion model that is temporally consistent (future actions do not affect generated past) for simulating target subpopulations.

subject: digital twin validation on HeartSteps
object: reproduces structure better than simpler simulators
statement: The paper shows that the digital twin reproduces the target subpopulation's temporal and between-participant structure better than simpler simulators at each pre-deployment stage of HeartSteps.

subject: MemTools agent memory research framework
statement: The paper introduces MemTools, an interoperability research framework that decouples memory system components from underlying deployment environments through declarative data contracts.

subject: MemTools memory lifecycle standardization
object: enables systematic isolation of memory variables
statement: The paper demonstrates that MemTools provides a practical infrastructure for advancing principled research on agent memory by enabling systematic isolation and analysis of memory design variables.

subject: Möbius RoPE positional encoding
object: anti-periodic frequency ladder for positional encoding
statement: The paper introduces Möbius RoPE, a rotary positional encoding built on the anti-periodic frequency ladder where every rotation plane advances by an odd multiple of π.

subject: needle-in-haystack retrieval reliability
statement: The paper reports that needle-in-haystack retrieval with Möbius RoPE reaches 90.3±5.7% versus 63.3±31.4% at context 512 (n=6 seeds).

subject: Möbius perplexity and generalization
statement: The paper shows that hybrid Möbius RoPE perplexity remains unchanged (29.66 vs. 29.72) while providing improved retrieval reliability.

subject: neural surrogates for tokamak plasmas
object: cycle-consistent U-Net forward with inverse optimization
statement: The paper introduces a cycle-consistent neural surrogate combining a conditional U-Net forward model with an optimization-based inverse method for tokamak edge plasma prediction.

subject: tokamak plasma field prediction accuracy
statement: The paper reports that the forward model achieves normalized root-mean-square errors below 2.6% and Pearson correlations above 0.95 for all predicted plasma-state fields.

subject: tokamak surrogate computational speedup
statement: The paper shows that with approximately 4×10^6 parameters, the model produces full 2D predictions in milliseconds, five to six orders of magnitude faster than SOLPS-ITER.

subject: parameterized quantum circuits generalization
statement: The paper shows that gradient-based parameterized quantum circuits can exhibit improved performance on unseen data as model size increases, displaying the double descent phenomenon.

subject: deep quantum circuits scaling behavior
object: larger models do not degrade generalization
statement: The paper provides analytical results demonstrating that deeper parameterized quantum circuits do not necessarily exhibit degraded performance as model depth increases.

subject: Euclid-MCP neuro-symbolic reasoning server
object: MCP server for SWI-Prolog deterministic reasoning
statement: The paper introduces Euclid-MCP, an open-source Model Context Protocol server providing deterministic logical reasoning via SWI-Prolog.

subject: Euclid-IR intermediate representation
statement: The paper introduces Euclid-IR, an engine-agnostic intermediate representation for Horn-clause logic that is human-readable and straightforward to compile into Prolog or alternative backends.

subject: neuro-symbolic reasoning comparison with LLMs
object: exact answers with lower latency than LLMs
statement: The paper shows that Euclid-MCP delivers exact answers with lower latency and more compact outputs compared to LLMs alone on IT security and compliance tasks.

subject: logical regression with axioms in planning
object: approximates regression limiting to partial states
statement: The paper introduces a methodology for approximating logical regression of actions in domains with axioms by limiting conditions to minimal partial states.

subject: execution monitoring variable reduction
statement: The paper demonstrates that embedded regression can dramatically reduce variables considered for execution monitoring by up to 70% across multiple domains.

subject: execution monitor robustness to changes
statement: The paper shows that the resulting execution monitor is robust enough to recover over 50% of the time in environments with unexpected changes.

subject: PATS policy-centric training for LLM agents
statement: The paper proposes PATS, a policy-centric training paradigm that reframes skills as a dynamic training scaffold for agentic reinforcement learning.

subject: training scaffold effectiveness on navigation
object: improves by up to 18.6% on ALFWorld and WebShop
statement: The paper shows that PATS improves over strong baselines by up to 18.6% on ALFWorld and WebShop navigation and interaction benchmarks.

subject: prompt token efficiency in QA
statement: The paper reports that PATS remains competitive across seven search-augmented QA benchmarks while using 32.1% fewer prompt tokens than the baseline.
